'''Yanagihara Shrine''' (やなぎはらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Kitadamachi, {{ill|Mishima, Shizuoka|Q653478|qid=Q653478}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}.

=== Overview ===
It is enshrined southwest of {{ill|Mishima Taisha|Q650772|qid=Q650772}}, along {{ill|Shizuoka Prefectural Road Route 21|Q11663360|qid=Q11663360|lt=Prefectural Route 21}}, just to the southwest of Mishima City Hall.

Yanagihara Shrine is a disputed candidate for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and it is also identified with the “Junior First Rank Yakiwara no Myōjin” listed in the {{ill|Izu Province Shrine Rank Register|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}. As for its founding, there are two theories: one holds that it was established as a branch shrine or distant worship site of the original shrine located at the present {{ill|Numazu|Q241037|qid=Q241037}} (Kanuki), namely {{ill|Yohara Shrine|Q11541065|qid=Q11541065}}; the other holds that it was relocated here after the original shrine’s precinct was incorporated into Suruga Province<ref name="sh">[https://shrineheritager.com/yanagihara-shrine/amp/ Yanagihara Shrine] - Shrine Heritager</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140214-02.html Yanagihara Shrine] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

It was formerly a {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}} (subsidiary shrine) of Mishima Taisha. Additionally, when {{ill|Sengen Shrine (Izu Province Ni-no-Miya)|Q30925511|qid=Q30925511|lt=Asama Shrine}}, which had originally been the Sannomiya of Izu Province, was promoted to Ninomiya, Yanagihara Shrine is said to have been promoted to Sannomiya. The shrine itself also claims the title of Sannomiya of Izu Province<ref name="sh"/><ref name="engi"/>.

Until the early Edo period, the shrine was located to the west of its current site, across the Gotengawa River. It is said to have been relocated to its present location due to the construction of a palace for Tokugawa Iemitsu at the former site<ref name="sh"/><ref name="engi"/>.
